newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Monday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. The tender results for the 3 months and one-year treasury bill are coming up, but the likely impact will be on the two-year bond. Volume is moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.38/2.33 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 2.18/2.13 percent.
One-year closed at a yield of 2.35/2.30 percent against 2.15/2.10 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.05/99.10 from last Friday's close of S$99.20/99.25, September 2001 was unchanged from last Friday's close of S$96.50/96.60, and June 2003 at S$94.40/94.45 versus S$94.47/94.52.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-7/8 3-3/4 percent from last Friday's 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent.
